newsitem.title: POLAND: WARSAW BOURSE OUTLOOK HAZY NEXT WEEK AFTER SURGE.
newsitem.headline: WARSAW BOURSE OUTLOOK HAZY NEXT WEEK AFTER SURGE.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse pierced psychological resistance of 17,000 points this week, breaking into a territory where any scenario including a painful correction was possible, analysts said.

They said Friday's strong demand was likely to push the bourse to more highs early next week, but some analysts warned the increasing pace of the upride might signal the market might soon peak to plunge later in profit-taking.

"At some stage the growth could end with a painful fall, but it's difficult to say when...the market seems to be in such a frenzy that everything is possible," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska.
He said both more rapid grows and a deep correction were possible next week.
The main market's all-share WIG index surged 8.4 percent this week to a 34-month high of 17,457.9 points on Friday.

Some analysts said the current average P/E ratio of 15.8 made Polish stocks fairly valued, but said the market remained attractive because of high 1997 earnings growth forecasts and good overall prospects of the Polish economy.

This week's resignation of finance minister Grzegorz Kolodko and his replacement with presidential aide Marek Belka did not affect stock prices but analysts said investors would be watching carefully the new minister's policy.

They said initial public offerings of electrodes maker Zaklady Elektrod Weglowych SA (ZEW) and trading and finacial firm BEST SA, worth a total of about 80 million zlotys, should not weight much on the market's sentiment.
Analysts said Optimus 18.6-percent jump this week was helped by Thursday's news it would exchange 159 of its convertible bonds into shares, boosting its January pre-tax by 1.3 million zlotys.

They said Mostostal Krakow and Elektrobudowa construction firms outperformed the market with 25.7 percent and 18.9 percent gains respectively, benefitting from the overall bullish outlook for the construction industry.
They said the 25 percent surge of another top performer Novita was a natural reaction to last week's 11.6 percent plunge, additionally helped by an upward revision of its profit forecast.
